sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between the Exodus from Egypt and the future redemption, noting that in Egypt evil was still at full strength requiring weapons, while in the future the spirit of impurity will be removed.

translations.translation: And based on this, the difference between the redemption from Egypt and the future redemption will be understood,
that although regarding the future redemption it is written "and they shall beat their swords into plowshares,"
nevertheless,
regarding the redemption from Egypt it is written "and the children of Israel went up armed,"
and this is because regarding the future it is written,
"and the spirit of impurity I will remove from the land,"
but not so regarding the redemption from Egypt, where evil was still at its full strength,
as explained in Tanya
regarding the matter of "for the people fled,"
that this is because evil was at its full strength,
except that since the redemption had to be in the blink of an eye,
they did not want to engage
(occupy themselves)
with this,
and since there was still evil, therefore they needed weapons,
but not so regarding the future, when "the spirit of impurity I will remove from the land,"
then "they shall beat their swords into plowshares."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section describes the two levels in the future redemption—in time and in soul—where initially there will still be a need for weapons, but ultimately the spirit of impurity will be removed and there will be peace through the King Moshiach.

translations.translation: And behold, in the future redemption there will be,
in general,
two levels,
in time and also in the soul.
For the people of the land, or as stated in Igeres HaKodesh regarding the mixed multitude,
and at the beginning of the time of the redemption it will be so for all of Israel,
in the manner of the statement of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,
"There is no difference between this world and the days of Moshiach except subjugation to the kingdoms alone," and there will be a need for a sword, etc.,
however, Torah scholars, and as stated in Igeres HaKodesh regarding Israel who are not of the mixed multitude,
and afterward it will be so for the general public,
when "the spirit of impurity I will remove from the land," they will not need a sword,
and concerning this it is said "and they shall beat their swords into plowshares," etc.
And this is the meaning of the verse "the exaltation of G-d is in their throat and a double-edged sword in their hand,"
for although it speaks of the future to come,
as stated at the opening of the psalm "Sing to G-d a new song, His praise in the assembly of the pious," and as mentioned above,
nevertheless, at the beginning of the time of the redemption there will be a need for weapons.
And concerning this it says that there will be "the exaltation of G-d in their throat and a double-edged sword in their hand,"
"to execute vengeance upon the nations,"
that the nations will still exist before they are refined to serve Him with a united shoulder,
and also in the manner explained in Likkutei Torah
on the verse "all nations surrounded me,"
which refers to "the nation that is within you,"
the body and the animal soul,
and they will need a double-edged sword in their hand.
And afterward, in the completeness of the redemption, "they shall beat their swords into plowshares, etc., and nation shall not lift up sword against nation,"
for "the spirit of impurity I will remove from the land,"
"and I will grant peace in the land,"
through the Prince of Peace,
Dovid,
the King Moshiach,
in the future redemption,
speedily in our days.
